source_title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework AI RMF 1.0
claim_supported: Defines a voluntary use-case-agnostic AI risk-management framework and supports governed documented role-aware lifecycle risk work without prescribing one technical architecture.
limitations: AI RMF 1.0 is voluntary non-sector-specific and currently under revision; it does not certify this method establish compliance or prove an AI system trustworthy.

claim_supported: Provides voluntary suggested actions aligned to Govern Map Measure and Manage including differentiated human-AI oversight roles and tracked risk information.
limitations: Mutable companion rather than a fixed checklist; NIST says the Playbook will be updated after the AI RMF revision and organizations tailor suggestions to context.

claim_supported: Supports governance risk context profiles and organizationally selected outcomes while separating a framework outcome from a prescribed implementation.
limitations: Cybersecurity risk framework only; it does not prescribe this self-storage policy architecture prove implementation or establish a certification.

source_title: Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations SP 800-53 Rev. 5
publication_or_version_date: Rev. 5 final 2020-12-10; planning note cites Release 5.2.0 on 2025-08-27
claim_supported: Supports selecting and tailoring access control audit accountability configuration management assessment monitoring and other controls through an organization-wide risk process.
limitations: Federal control catalog that is flexible and customizable; the page does not require every listed control for a private operator or prove any control is implemented effectively.

claim_supported: Supports separating a policy decision mechanism policy administration and policy enforcement and avoiding implicit trust based only on location or ownership.
limitations: Zero-trust cybersecurity architecture not a complete facility operating model; it does not determine business authority physical-safety rules or accounting treatment.

source_title: eXtensible Access Control Markup Language XACML Version 3.0
claim_supported: Provides a stable standards-based reference for separating policy administration information decision and enforcement roles and for returning permit deny indeterminate or not-applicable decisions.
limitations: Access-control standard rather than a self-storage implementation recipe; terminology is adapted as an architectural reference and does not establish legal authority or safe physical action.

claim_supported: Describes OPA as a general-purpose policy decision point serving application enforcement points and identifies policy loading external data and decision logging as distinct responsibilities.
limitations: OPA-specific and mutable; cited as an implementation example not a required provider universal standard product relationship or released Facily architecture.

claim_supported: Documents decision IDs policy query inputs results bundle revision metadata trace fields and masking mechanisms that can support audit and replay-oriented design.
limitations: OPA-specific logging behavior only; logging may expose sensitive inputs unless governed and a decision log does not prove authority enforcement correctness safety or outcome.
